chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding a man who treads upon a place that is not clean, then treads after it on a clean place, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if it is fifteen cubits or thereabouts.'
ai.seo_question: How many cubits must one walk on a clean surface to purify their feet after stepping on impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the principle of 'removal of impurity through walking' (taharah bi al-mashi), specifying that approximately fifteen cubits of travel on a clean surface suffices to cleanse the feet from feces or similar filth. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a practical application of the general rule that impurities on movable objects are removed by traversing a sufficient distance, reflecting the ease (taysir) intended in ritual purification.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Al Ahowl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding the man who trod upon the place which was not with cleanliness, then he trod after it in a clean place, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem when it was fifteen cubits away or approximate to that (i.e. sufficient walking would purify it)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih from al-Ahwal who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one steps on a spot which is unclean, then steps on a clean spot, it is not harmful after walking a distance of fifteen yards or so.’”
